content:
sara-support: Hey team — customer acme-corp reporting frequent SSE disconnects on long streaming responses. They see partial outputs and mobile clients log write errors then reconnect. Started after an app update yesterday. Attaching repro and logs.

kevin-sre: Which endpoint and region? Any correlation with response size or client network type?

sara-support: Endpoint is /v1/streams/generate on hosted. Symptoms mostly when generation > ~15s or payload > ~10k tokens. Edge snippet they supplied: 
```
[2026-03-14T18:22:11Z] conn=abcd123 write error: EAGAIN
[2026-03-14T18:22:11Z] conn=abcd123 write error: EPIPE
[2026-03-14T18:22:11Z] stream aborted by server: short write
```
Client sees socket close and ECONNRESET. They use a mobile SDK with flaky networks.

maya-eng: Sounds like slow consumer/backpressure. If the client's read loop is slow the kernel send buffer fills, our runtime gets EAGAIN or EPIPE depending on state. Are we doing blocking writes currently?

kevin-sre: Runtime flushes in 4KB chunks per token batch and will block up to 500ms, then we abort after our safeguard (configured 1s). That matches observed server aborts. If many streams are stalled we risk head-of-line blocking on the worker.

sara-support: Customer wants reconnect+resume rather than full abort. They also reported duplicate billing because reconnect is treated as a new request. Nina, heads up on billing impact.

nina-billing: Noted. Billing dedupe currently relies on Idempotency-Key header, which most streaming clients don't set. Recommend advising clients to send an idempotency header for long-running streams.

maya-eng: Immediate mitigations for customer: 1) implement client auto-reconnect with idempotency-key so server can dedupe; 2) reduce per-request batch size in client to limit burst writes; 3) ensure client keeps small read heartbeat to avoid being classified as slow. Long term we should: implement non-blocking writes + bounded per-client buffer and surface a 'buffer-pressure' metric.

kevin-sre: Also check proxy buffering: if envoy/nginx in front buffers upstream responses then a slow downstream can cause upstream to back up. For hosted customers we use envoy with stream_idle_timeout. We should set route buffer limits to 'none' for streaming endpoints and increase stream_idle_timeout.

sara-support: I made a tiny curl-based repro that simulates slow consumer by sleeping between event reads: 
```
curl -N 'https://api.redwood.dev/v1/streams/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"prompt":"very long prompt...","stream":true}' | \
  awk 'BEGIN{RS="";RS="\n\n"} {print; system("sleep 1")}'
```
This reproduces the EAGAIN and eventual abort within seconds in staging.

kevin-sre: I'll run that on staging with tcpdump and collect `ss -tnp` and per-socket sndq values. We should also log SO_SNDBUF and pending bytes when a write fails to correlate.

maya-eng: Dev plan: 
- short term: increase envoy stream_idle_timeout to 75s and disable buffering on streaming route; bump net.core.wmem_max on streaming nodes if safe.
- medium term: add non-blocking write path, maintain a bounded in-memory buffer per client (max 256KB), and increment a per-client counter when kernel send queue grows. If buffer limits hit, mark stream as stalled and emit 'client_slow' metric.
- long term: introduce resume tokens in SSE payloads and support resume semantics (client reconnect with last-ack token). Also expose X-Client-Buffer-Pressure header for visibility.

kevin-sre: I'll also add an alert: if write-error rate on streaming nodes > 5% for 10m, page oncall and attach the runbook. Will capture existing nodes' wmem settings.

sara-support: For the customer immediate workaround I will tell them: implement reconnect with idempotency-key, add small periodic reads to keep socket draining, and set socket keepalive. Also ask them to report SDK version so we can check read loop performance.

sre-bot: :robot_face: Created alert STREAM_WRITE_ERRORS_HIGH for streaming-prod. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.dev/runbooks/stream-write-errors.

maya-eng: One more note: when we abort we currently return 499 or a closed connection without a clear last-state. We should, if possible, emit an X-Last-Token header with the last-ack index before closing so clients can resume.

sara-support: Thanks everyone. I'll email acme-corp with the short-term steps and follow up once kevin shares staging traces. :eyes: :thumbsup:
